extracted.intended_audience: general readers and historians interested in the history and critique of the Illuminati/Free Masonry and 18th-century secret societies
extracted.subtask_description: A polemical/historical account describing the principles, rituals, recruitment tactics, and secretive organization of the Illuminati and related Masonic systems, with extracts from internal correspondence and ritual texts. Focus is on revealing the order's aims and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use religion as a cloak to promote Reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Philo and Spartacus describe Christianity (and other popular religious forms) as a 'cloak' to prevent squeamish people from starting back; secret doctrines of Reason are wrapped up in popular religion and taught by parables, disclosed only to a chosen few.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine secret doctrines with existing religious customs and rituals to gain acceptance; teach the masses in parables while revealing the true meaning only to initiates. This method is explicitly practical: it secures a patient hearing and prevents immediate rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gradually explain away preparatory pious frauds
rubrics_metrics.description: Spartacus: 'We must, 1st, gradually explain away all our preparatory pious frauds.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When criticized, plead the good end of the Order's labour to sanctify ambiguous or deceptive methods; use ambiguous expressions to elicit responses and discover pupils' minds before revealing fuller doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfold the origin and fabrication of religious lies; publish a critical history of the Order
rubrics_metrics.description: Spartacus: '2d, We must unfold, from history and other writings, the origin and fabrication of all religious lies whatever; and then, 3d, We give a critical history of the Order.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical and literary exposition to undermine existing religious beliefs and to justify the Order's doctrines; produce critical accounts of the Order itself for internal or strategic use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain doctrines via Disciplina Arcani among Adepti
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctrines of Christianity (as used by the Order) were committed to the Adepti in a 'Disciplina Arcani'; secrets were kept in hidden societies, handed down with degrees of information (a seventy, a twelve), preserved like a Vestal Fire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve core teachings in secret levels; restrict full knowledge to higher ranks and conserve continuity through ritual and restricted transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hidden societies/schools as the vehicle for liberation and union
rubrics_metrics.description: Spartacus: hidden schools of wisdom are the means which will one day free men from their bonds; hidden societies unite men and act as archives of natural rights and the means to raise human nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize clandestine networks to educate and morally reform members, creating self-governing individuals and ultimately abolishing external despotisms through gradual moral and intellectual transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish preparatory literature (including fictitious antiquities) to prepare minds
rubrics_metrics.description: Weishaupt published a fictitious antique ('Sidonii Apollinarus Fragmenta') to prepare minds for doctrines of Reason; similar publications and anonymous pamphlets were used to show that Free Masonry was Christianity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use printed works—including pseudepigrapha or forged antiquities and anonymous pamphlets—to acclimatize the public to new doctrines and to lower resistance to the Order's ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruit and control via infiltration of Masonic lodges and selection of officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Knigge's strategy: introduce the Eclectic System among Masons and bring Lodges under Illuminati direction by influencing the choice of the Master and Wardens; aim to notice conduct of individuals, find those fit for purpose, and gain them over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work within existing organizations (Free Masonry) to place sympathetic leadership, observe and vet candidates, and progressively bring lodges into the Order's orbit without obvious detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquire influence and funds within lodges subtly
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Scotch Knight: 'He must endeavour to acquire the possession of considerable property. In all Mason Lodges we must try secretly to get the upper hand... We must endeavour to get the disposal of the money of the Lodges of the Free Masons.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gain financial resources and administrative control within target institutions through covert means so as to apply lodge assets in ways favourable to the Order while avoiding detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bind members by ritual, degrees, bonds, and oaths
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order uses a graded system of degrees, bonds, and oaths (e.g., candidate binds himself 'for ever to the Order'); oaths include commitments such as opposing superstition and despotism, reporting progress, and considering the Illuminati as superiors of Free Masonry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ elaborate rituals, fixed degrees, and legally/ceremonially framed bonds to secure members' loyalty and silence, and to make their social/economic lives dependent on the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use initiation dilemmas and ensnaring questions to test and prepare candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare candidates by bringing them into dilemmas by 'ensnaring questions' so as to reveal their dispositions; make them sign bonds only after they are committed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probe recruits' beliefs and loyalties through staged questioning and progressive commitments to ensure they are suitable and then finalize their subjection via oaths and bonds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploit women and female societies as vectors of influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Minos proposes a Minerval school for girls to 'improve the world' by influencing women—'They will be our great apostles.' The plan: create female societies with degrees, rituals, and mystery to inspire enthusiasm and spread doctrine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form all-female societies with attractive ceremonies and autonomy (men out of sight) so they invent mystique and evangelize men; be mindful of risks (women seen as fickle) but exploit their social influence where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use symbolic communal rituals (e.g., Love-Feast) to cement internal unity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Love-Feast ritual: a Table Lodge with a covered chalice, unleavened bread, an unveiling, and a recited narrative linking the ceremony to Jesus as Grand-Master; presented as 'the mark of our Holy Union.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and perform communal, symbolic rites that create emotional bonding and doctrinal identification among members under the guise of antiquity or shared moral purpose.
